transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess they brought me in because of work. At the warehouse. People keep saying I’m acting weird around the forklifts and the pallets and all that, but it’s hard to explain because when it’s happening it doesn’t feel like I’m trying to make a scene.

Like I’ll be by the forklift and I’ll just sort of freeze there with my arms up, like I’m holding a sign or stopping traffic or something, and I can hear people yelling, but I don’t move right away. Or the forklift makes that backing-up beep and I’ll start copying it, like “beep… beep… beep,” and sometimes I copy the hand signals the guys use, even when I’m not the one guiding anything. And then with the boxes, I’ll start moving them into these little patterns, like lining them up or making them go a certain way, even if that’s not where they’re supposed to go.

They get mad because it slows everything down, and they’re yelling at me to stop, but I keep doing it for a bit. So… yeah, I think that’s why I’m here.

Have you ever had episodes like this before—freezing up, repeating sounds or gestures, arranging things in patterns—earlier in your life, say as a child or teenager, or is this something that's only started recently?

I don’t really remember it being like this when I was a kid or even in high school. I mean, I might’ve had little habits, like everybody does, but not where people were stopping work and yelling or saying I was talking confusing or acting strange.

This warehouse stuff has been more recent… but not just, like, last week. It’s been going on for about six months, I think. Around that long. At first I thought it was just bad days or being tired, and then it kept happening, and people started noticing more because I’d get stuck or repeat things or do the patterns with the boxes, and then I guess the way I talk about it doesn’t come out right either. So… yeah, about six months now.
Have you been hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having beliefs that other people say aren't true, around the time these episodes happen?

I don’t know… I mean, not really in the way people talk about it, like a voice standing behind me saying my name or telling me things. I don’t think so. Sometimes at work there’s so much noise — the beeping, the metal shelves, people shouting across the floor — that it’s hard to tell what I’m hearing versus what’s just in the building, you know?

Like with the forklift beep, I hear that because everybody hears that. And then I get sort of stuck on it and I repeat it, but I’m not sure that’s the same as hearing something nobody else hears. Nobody’s said, “There’s no sound,” or anything like that. It’s more like they say, “Stop copying it,” or “Get out of the way.”

As far as beliefs… I don’t know. People tell me I’m wrong about what I’m doing, like that the boxes don’t need to be arranged that way or that I’m making the job harder, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I’m not walking around with some big idea that everyone says is impossible. At least I don’t think I am. It’s more confusing in the moment than anything.
Have you had any recent medical problems, head injuries, seizures, or been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these episodes started?

Um… I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I don’t have, like, a clear thing I can point to and say, “That’s when it started.” Nobody told me, like, “You had a seizure,” or anything like that. I don’t think there was some big accident or something that lines up with it.

As far as medical stuff, I mean… I haven’t really been keeping track the way maybe I should. I go to work, come home, sleep weird sometimes, eat whatever, and then the next day it’s kind of the same. So I don’t know if there was a medical problem I didn’t notice. But I don’t have some obvious thing in my mind.

Drugs or alcohol… I don’t really know what counts as important there. I’m not trying to hide anything, I just don’t have a clear answer that feels connected to the warehouse stuff. And new medications—nothing is jumping out to me. I’d have to think about it or maybe someone in my family would remember better, because the past few months feel kind of blurred together.
During these episodes, are you aware of what’s happening around you and able to remember it afterward, or do you find that you can’t recall parts of what happened once it’s over?

I’m… not totally sure. I think I’m aware, mostly, like I know I’m in the warehouse and I know people are around me and I can hear when someone is annoyed or trying to get my attention. It’s not like I wake up somewhere else and have no idea how I got there.

But afterward it gets kind of muddy. I can remember pieces, like the sound or the boxes or somebody saying my name, but the order of it is hard to put together. Sometimes I only realize how long it must’ve gone on because people are looking at me differently, or a supervisor is already upset, and I’m trying to figure out what part I missed. So I don’t know if that counts as not remembering, because I do remember some of it, but not cleanly. It’s more like… I was there, but I wasn’t keeping track of everything right.

Do these episodes tend to happen after something stressful or upsetting occurs—like an argument, a demand from a supervisor, or feeling overwhelmed—or do they seem to come on regardless of what’s going on emotionally at the time?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clean pattern like that. I mean, sometimes the warehouse is just a lot — not even one specific thing, just all of it happening at once, people moving fast, noises, somebody needing something, and I’m trying to keep up. So maybe that counts as overwhelmed, but it’s hard for me to say, “This happened because I got upset,” you know?

I don’t always remember there being an argument first or a supervisor saying something before it starts. Sometimes I only realize people are irritated after I’m already doing whatever I’m doing. Other times, yeah, if someone is on me or there’s pressure, I get more tense, but I don’t know if that’s the trigger or if I’m just noticing it more because everybody is looking at me.

It kind of feels like it comes on with the situation, but not always because I’m emotionally upset in a way I can name. It’s more like I get caught in the middle of everything, and then later I’m trying to figure out what set it off, and I can’t really point to one thing.

During these freezing episodes, if someone tries to move your arms or reposition you, do they find your limbs stay stiff or hold whatever position they're put in, or do they move your body without any resistance?

I don’t really know about the arm-moving part exactly. People don’t usually calmly come over and test it like that, or at least I don’t remember it that way. What I know is what they tell me afterward, and what I kind of remember in pieces.

Like, I’ll be by the forklift and I guess I freeze with my arms up, almost like I’m stuck in the middle of doing one of the hand signals or something. And then people are yelling, because obviously that’s not what I’m supposed to be doing there. Sometimes I’m copying the forklift beeping noises or the hand signals, and I know that sounds stupid when I say it out loud, but in the moment it feels like I’m just… locked into it.

The boxes thing happens too, where instead of moving them how I’m supposed to, I start putting them in these weird little patterns, like lining them up or shifting them back and forth in a way that doesn’t make sense to anyone else. People tell me to stop, and I guess I don’t stop right away, even when they’re getting mad.

So, if you mean do I go stiff like a board if someone touches me, I don’t know for sure. I just know I kind of freeze or get stuck doing these strange movements, and other people have to snap me out of it or get really loud before I come back to what I’m supposed to be doing.
Do these freezing and repeating episodes ever happen outside of work—like at home, with family, or in other situations—or have they only occurred at the warehouse?

Mostly it’s been at the warehouse. I mean, that’s the place everyone keeps pointing to when they tell me something’s wrong, because that’s where I’ll get stuck doing things I’m not supposed to be doing — like freezing with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeping sounds and the hand signals, or moving the boxes into these weird little patterns instead of just doing the job.

At home, I don’t really have forklifts and supervisors and people yelling across the floor, so it’s hard to compare. I’m not saying nothing ever feels strange anywhere else, but the actual episodes people keep bringing up, the ones where they say I’m frozen or repeating things and not stopping even when they’re yelling at me — that’s been at work, as far as I know. That’s why they got worried, I guess, because it was happening there where it can mess things up or be dangerous.

I’m not sure what else to say beyond that, honestly. Like, I can tell you what people at work have told me, and I can tell you the parts I remember, but if you’re asking whether I know for sure it happens in other places too, I don’t really know.

At home, there isn’t the same kind of setup where someone would be watching me and saying, “Hey, you froze,” or “You’re repeating that,” you know? If I’m just sitting there or walking around, I don’t know if it would even stand out the same way. At the warehouse it’s obvious because I’m supposed to be doing something specific and there are machines and boxes and people waiting on me, so when I stop or get stuck, everybody notices.

So I guess my answer is: as far as I know, the episodes they’re worried about have been at work. I don’t have a clear memory of the same thing happening at home or somewhere else, but I also don’t totally trust that I’d notice it the same way if nobody pointed it out.

Aside from these specific episodes at work, have people close to you noticed any other changes over the past several months—like you becoming more withdrawn, losing interest in things you used to care about, or your speech or thinking seeming disorganized even when you're not frozen or repeating things?

Yeah… people have said my talking gets hard to follow, even when I’m not frozen or doing the repeating thing. I don’t always notice it while I’m saying it, because in my head it feels like I’m answering, like I’m giving the whole explanation, but then everyone looks at me like I didn’t answer at all.

Like at work, my supervisor will ask something simple, like which pallets are going on the truck. And I’ll start trying to explain from the load sheet, because that’s what I’m supposed to be talking about, but then I’ll somehow get onto my old house, because the numbers on the sheet remind me of the address or the garage or something, and then I’ll mention fishing because there were pallets by the bait freezer one time, or I don’t know, it connects in my head. Then somehow I’m talking about church boxes, like boxes people use for donations, and by the time I stop talking, nobody knows which pallets I meant.

And I can see them getting frustrated, like, “Just answer the question,” but I thought I was answering it. That’s the part that bothers me. I’m not trying to be difficult or funny. It’s like the words take side roads and I follow them, and then I can’t get back to the main road fast enough.

Yeah, that’s the main thing people notice, I think — my talking doesn’t stay where it’s supposed to stay.

Like, if my supervisor asks me which pallets are supposed to go on the truck, it should be easy. I know that. It’s not a hard question. But I’ll look at the load sheet and start explaining it, and then the numbers or something on it make me think of my old house, like the address or the garage, and then I’m talking about that for some reason. Then that reminds me of fishing, because of a freezer or a place we used to go, and then somehow I get onto church boxes, like donation boxes or boxes stacked up in a church hallway, and by the time I’m finished talking, everyone’s just staring at me.

And I can tell they don’t know what I meant. They’ll be like, “Which pallets?” and I realize I never really answered it, even though in my head I was trying to. It feels connected while I’m saying it, but when it comes out, I guess it sounds like I’m jumping all over the place. That’s been happening even when I’m not frozen or repeating stuff. It’s just how my words come out sometimes, and it makes people frustrated with me.

Outside of these specific work episodes, have you or others noticed a change in your emotions—like feeling flat or numb, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or pulling away from friends and family over these past several months?

I don’t really know how to answer that one cleanly. I mean, I hear what you’re asking, but I don’t know if I can say, like, “Yes, this changed on this day,” or anything like that.

I guess people might think I’m quieter sometimes, but I don’t always feel like I’m trying to pull away. Sometimes I’m just tired, or I don’t know what to say, or I’m worried if I start talking it’s going to come out wrong and then I’ll have to explain the explanation. So I might just not say much. But I don’t know if that’s the same thing as being numb or flat.

As far as losing interest in stuff, I don’t know. I haven’t really been keeping track. Some things feel like too much effort, but then again work takes a lot out of me, and when I get home I’m mostly just trying to get through the rest of the day. I’m not sure if other people see that as me not caring anymore.

So… maybe there’s been some of that, but I can’t really tell you for sure. I don’t have a clear answer like I do with people telling me my talking gets off track.

Over the past six months, have you noticed any physical symptoms like fevers, unexplained weight changes, tremors, excessive sweating, or times when your heart was racing or blood pressure seemed off, that happened around the same time as these episodes?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’ve really noticed. I mean, I get hot or sweaty sometimes at work, but that’s because I’m moving freight and lifting stuff, and the warehouse gets hot, so I don’t know that I’d count that as something happening with the episodes.

I haven’t been checking my blood pressure or anything like that, so I can’t really say if it was “off.” And with my heart racing… sometimes if I’m stressed or embarrassed after something happens, it feels like my chest is kind of worked up, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean or if that’s just me being anxious because people are staring at me.

I haven’t noticed fevers. I don’t have, like, a record of my weight or anything, so I’m not sure about changes there. No one’s told me I look really different, at least not that I can remember. Tremors… I don’t think I’ve had shaking like that. Not that stands out.

So I guess my answer is mostly no, or I’m not sure. I haven’t really connected anything physical like that to when the episodes happen.

Over these past six months, have you or others noticed times when you seem more confused, drowsy, or 'foggy'—like your alertness comes and goes during the day—separate from the specific freezing episodes at work?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed it like that, no. Not like I’m half-asleep in the middle of the day or people are saying I’m not alert. I mean, I get tired, but I think most people get tired, especially after work or when I haven’t slept great or when the day is just long.

When you say “foggy,” I’m trying to figure out if you mean like confused about where I am or not knowing what’s going on, because I don’t think it’s that. I can be mixed up in what I’m saying, or I can lose the thread of what I was supposed to be doing if there’s too much going on, but I don’t think my alertness is, like, coming in and out. At least nobody has told me that in those words.

So… I guess I’d say not really, or not separately from the work stuff. If it’s happening, I’m not catching it that way.

Have you had any recent blood tests, brain imaging (like an MRI or CT scan), or been told you have a medical condition—such as thyroid problems, an infection, or an autoimmune disease—that could be related to these episodes?

I don’t think I’ve had anything like that recently. Not that I can remember, anyway. I mean, I’ve had regular doctor stuff before, but I haven’t gone in and had, like, a scan of my head or anything where they said, “This explains what’s happening.”

Blood tests… maybe at some point in my life, but not recently for this. Nobody has told me, “Your thyroid is off,” or “You have an infection,” or “This is autoimmune,” or anything like that. If they did, I think I would remember because that sounds like the kind of thing they’d make a big deal out of.

I also haven’t really been going to doctors a lot for these episodes, so it’s not like there’s been a whole workup that came back normal or abnormal. It’s more like… things have been happening, and I’ve been trying to get through them, and then people started noticing more, and now I’m here talking about it.

So, no, I don’t have a medical condition that I know of that someone has connected to it, and I haven’t had an MRI or CT scan or recent blood tests for it.

Have you noticed yourself holding any strong beliefs that others have told you aren't true or don't make sense—like thinking people are watching you, plotting against you, or that you have special powers or a special mission?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I don’t think I have special powers or some mission, not like that. And I don’t think I’m sitting around making a plan around it or anything.

People do tell me sometimes I’m reading too much into things, or that something probably doesn’t mean anything, and I can kind of hear that when they say it, but in the moment it can feel different. Like if someone is looking over or talking quietly, I might wonder if it has to do with me, but I don’t know if that counts as a “strong belief” or just me being uncomfortable. I don’t want to say yes to something that sounds bigger than what I mean.

I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed having one fixed belief that everybody keeps telling me is false. Not like, “everyone is plotting against me” in a clear way. Sometimes I worry about what people think or whether they’re watching me, but then I also question myself afterward, so… I don’t know. It’s not something I’m completely sure about.
Does anyone in your family—parents, siblings, or other close relatives—have a history of schizophrenia, psychosis, or other serious mental illness?

I’m not really sure. I mean, not that I know of in the close-family way, like my parents or siblings telling me they were diagnosed with something like that. My family doesn’t really talk about mental health very openly, so it’s possible there are things I just don’t know, or people called it something else, or nobody went to a doctor for it.

I’ve heard little comments here and there over the years, like someone was “having a hard time” or “not doing right,” but I don’t know what that actually meant, and I don’t want to turn that into some official thing when nobody ever said that to me. Nobody sat me down and said, “Your uncle has this,” or “Your mom had that,” or anything clear like that.

So the honest answer is I don’t know of any history like that, but I also don’t know if I’d be the person in the family who would have been told.

I honestly don’t really know. Not in a clear way, anyway. My family isn’t the type that sits around and explains things like that, or says, “This person had this diagnosis,” you know? If something was going on with somebody, it would usually get talked about in a vague way, like they were “going through something” or they were “not themselves,” but nobody ever really spelled it out for me.

As far as my parents or siblings, nobody has told me they have anything like that. And I haven’t heard anything definite about close relatives either. I just don’t want to say no like I’m completely sure, because there could be stuff people didn’t talk about or didn’t get checked out. But from what I actually know, no, there isn’t a clear family history that I’ve been told about.
Sorry, I’m not sure I caught the question. Could you say that again? I think I was still thinking about the family history thing and kind of got stuck on it.
During these freezing episodes, has anyone ever noticed you having jerking or shaking movements, biting your tongue, or losing control of your bladder or bowels?

I don’t think so. I mean, nobody’s ever told me they saw me shaking or jerking around like that. When I freeze, from what I understand, it’s more like I just kind of get stuck, or I’m not responding right, but I don’t have someone filming me or watching every second, so I can’t say with total certainty.

I haven’t noticed anything like biting my tongue afterward, like blood or soreness that made me think that happened. And I don’t remember losing control of my bladder or bowels during it. That would probably really scare me, and I think I’d remember if that happened, or someone would have said something.

But yeah… as far as anyone noticing those things, no one has told me that. I’m not sure if they always know what to look for, though.

target_item.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior

patient.answer:
Yeah, um… I guess they brought me in because of work. At the warehouse. People keep saying I’m acting weird around the forklifts and the pallets and all that, but it’s hard to explain because when it’s happening it doesn’t feel like I’m trying to make a scene.

Like I’ll be by the forklift and I’ll just sort of freeze there with my arms up, like I’m holding a sign or stopping traffic or something, and I can hear people yelling, but I don’t move right away. Or the forklift makes that backing-up beep and I’ll start copying it, like “beep… beep… beep,” and sometimes I copy the hand signals the guys use, even when I’m not the one guiding anything. And then with the boxes, I’ll start moving them into these little patterns, like lining them up or making them go a certain way, even if that’s not where they’re supposed to go.

They get mad because it slows everything down, and they’re yelling at me to stop, but I keep doing it for a bit. So… yeah, I think that’s why I’m here.

inference.note: Initial presentation with echopraxia (mimicking hand signals), echolalia (mimicking beeping), posturing/freezing, and stereotyped patterning behavior suggests catatonic phenomena; differential includes catatonia (schizophrenia-associated or due to medical condition), autism spectrum with stereotypies, tic disorder with echophenomena, and dissociative/conversion-type motor phenomena.

doctor.intent: Determine whether these behaviors are a new development or something present since childhood, to distinguish acute-onset catatonic/psychotic phenomena from a lifelong neurodevelopmental pattern
doctor.question: Have you ever had episodes like this before—freezing up, repeating sounds or gestures, arranging things in patterns—earlier in your life, say as a child or teenager, or is this something that's only started recently?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking when the freezing, repeating sounds/gestures, and arranging behaviors began, which directly relates to how long these psychotic symptoms have been occurring.

patient.answer:
I don’t really remember it being like this when I was a kid or even in high school. I mean, I might’ve had little habits, like everybody does, but not where people were stopping work and yelling or saying I was talking confusing or acting strange.

This warehouse stuff has been more recent… but not just, like, last week. It’s been going on for about six months, I think. Around that long. At first I thought it was just bad days or being tired, and then it kept happening, and people started noticing more because I’d get stuck or repeat things or do the patterns with the boxes, and then I guess the way I talk about it doesn’t come out right either. So… yeah, about six months now.

inference.note: Absence of childhood-onset symptoms rules out F84.0 (autism) and F95.9 (tic disorder). patient.answer:
I don’t know… I mean, not really in the way people talk about it, like a voice standing behind me saying my name or telling me things. I don’t think so. Sometimes at work there’s so much noise — the beeping, the metal shelves, people shouting across the floor — that it’s hard to tell what I’m hearing versus what’s just in the building, you know?

Like with the forklift beep, I hear that because everybody hears that. And then I get sort of stuck on it and I repeat it, but I’m not sure that’s the same as hearing something nobody else hears. Nobody’s said, “There’s no sound,” or anything like that. It’s more like they say, “Stop copying it,” or “Get out of the way.”

As far as beliefs… I don’t know. People tell me I’m wrong about what I’m doing, like that the boxes don’t need to be arranged that way or that I’m making the job harder, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean. I’m not walking around with some big idea that everyone says is impossible. At least I don’t think I am. It’s more confusing in the moment than anything.

As far as medical stuff, I mean… I haven’t really been keeping track the way maybe I should. I go to work, come home, sleep weird sometimes, eat whatever, and then the next day it’s kind of the same. So I don’t know if there was a medical problem I didn’t notice. But I don’t have some obvious thing in my mind.

Drugs or alcohol… I don’t really know what counts as important there. I’m not trying to hide anything, I just don’t have a clear answer that feels connected to the warehouse stuff. And new medications—nothing is jumping out to me. I’d have to think about it or maybe someone in my family would remember better, because the past few months feel kind of blurred together.

I’m… not totally sure. I think I’m aware, mostly, like I know I’m in the warehouse and I know people are around me and I can hear when someone is annoyed or trying to get my attention. It’s not like I wake up somewhere else and have no idea how I got there.

Sometimes I only realize how long it must’ve gone on because people are looking at me differently, or a supervisor is already upset, and I’m trying to figure out what part I missed. It kind of feels like it comes on with the situation, but not always because I’m emotionally upset in a way I can name. It’s more like I get caught in the middle of everything, and then later I’m trying to figure out what set it off, and I can’t really point to one thing.

I don’t really know about the arm-moving part exactly. People don’t usually calmly come over and test it like that, or at least I don’t remember it that way. What I know is what they tell me afterward, and what I kind of remember in pieces.

And I can see them getting frustrated, like, “Just answer the question,” but I thought I was answering it. That’s the part that bothers me. I’m not trying to be difficult or funny. It’s like the words take side roads and I follow them, and then I can’t get back to the main road fast enough.
